### Constitution gates: all pass, no violations

Four structures exceed a bare script (package layout, one exception class, the planning pass, the written-path set) — each is justified in writing against the requirement that forces it, as Principle IV demands.

### Things worth your attention

- **The spec contradicts itself on one input.** With no `--overwrite`, a regular-file member, and a directory already at the target path: FR-019 says exit 3, FR-023 and the Edge Cases list say exit 2. I resolved it to **exit 2** (research R8) so that status 3 always means "re-run with `--overwrite`". This is the one behavior decided in the plan rather than the spec — consider amending the spec to match.
- **`tarfile.open(..., "r:*")` also accepts bzip2 and xz.** I kept it rather than restricting to gzip: the spec requires tar+gzip to work and never requires other formats to fail, and restricting would be *more* code. Flagged as a deliberate accepted superset.
- **`tarfile.ReadError` is multi-line and ugly** (it enumerates every compression method it tried). FR-027 wants one short line, so the design owns its own message catalogue instead of forwarding exception text.
- **`extractall` is not used.** It overwrites unconditionally, can't report a written-file count, and applies metadata the spec excludes — FR-019/020, FR-015/021 and FR-016/026 are unreachable through it. Writing members directly also sidesteps the version-dependent extraction-filter transition, keeping the 3.11+ floor real.
- Your three inputs are all honored: Python 3.11+ stdlib-only, the spec's interface verbatim (`contracts/cli-contract.md` is the normative restatement), and pytest with a `pytest.ini` so a bare `pytest` from the root works as the constitution requires.
